sections.html:
The offices you call depend on where the house sits. Greenburgh has six villages, and everything outside them is unincorporated town land. Greenburgh is in the west of Westchester, where the Hudson forms its border on one side, Yonkers lies below it, Mount Pleasant above, and White Plains and Scarsdale beside it. About half of residents live in villages. The rest live in unincorporated areas such as Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale, plus North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

The Building Department takes complaints only for the unincorporated area, and the Tax Department sends village residents to their own Village Hall for due dates. A seller in Tarrytown therefore checks two sets of offices, while a seller in Hartsdale deals mostly with the town.

Greenburgh had 94,537 residents in 2025 across 35,813 households, and owners occupy 74.0% of homes. The median home is worth $697,100. Renters pay $2,316 at the median, the middle household earns $152,256, and getting to work takes 34.4 minutes on average. At that price level, closing costs and the state's one percent charge on high-value homes both start to matter. If you are weighing a sale against renting the house out, that rent figure is the number to test.

Commuting questions come up first with buyers. Hudson Line trains of Metro-North stop at Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown, and Hartsdale has a Harlem Line station. Drivers have the Thruway, the Cross Westchester Expressway, the Saw Mill River, Bronx River and Sprain Brook parkways, US 9 and routes 9A, 100 and 119. The county's Bee-Line buses run here too.

Ten school districts feed into the tax office's billing, so the district printed on your bill can change the total between neighboring streets. Get your current bill in hand before pricing the house.

sections.h2: Building permits to check before listing
sections.html:
The Building Department's FAQ casts a wide net: building, fixing, improving, altering or tearing down anything calls for a permit. Re-roofing a one or two family house is included, and structural roof work needs drawings sealed by a New York State architect or engineer.

  • Sheds of any size need a permit. The limit is one per lot, placed in the rear yard, at most 150 square feet and 10 feet high.
  • Fences need no building permit up to six feet in a front or side yard and eight feet in the rear, with a 30 inch cap near corners.
  • Repaving an existing driveway needs nothing, but enlarging it does, and Public Works may also require a curb cut or right-of-way permit.
  • Pulling or abandoning a heating oil tank takes its own permit and inspection.
  • No residential zoning district lists short-term rentals as a permitted use.

If a buyer mentions a vacation rental, raise that last rule early. Bring or mail applications to 177 Hillside Avenue on a weekday. Current hours are posted on the forms page.

sections.h2: Property taxes and what happens at closing
sections.html:
One office, the Receiver of Taxes, sends bills covering the county, the town, the fire districts and ten school districts, making it the largest municipal collector in Westchester. Ask it for the next due date and a balance on paper before you close.

  • Checks go to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes, 177 Hillside Avenue. Paying online by card adds a fee that varies, and ACH payments cost nothing.
  • Liens are the exception: they can't be paid online.
  • Once title passes, the new owner should call so later bills find the right mailbox. If you've moved, send the office your forwarding address in writing.

State law adds two limits. Not receiving a bill doesn't wipe out the tax or its interest (Real Property Tax Law section 922), and the Receiver may not waive a penalty (section 920).

Greenburgh assessment and collection dates
DateWhat happens
June 1Tentative roll open for public viewing
Until September 15Appeals heard by the Board of Assessment Review
September 15Roll becomes final
January 31, April 30, September 30Receiver's office stays open until 7 p.m. on the final payment day

Once final, the roll is fixed, and later small claims changes don't alter it. Compare your own line with recent nearby sales. The buyer's attorney reads the same entry, and the Assessor's Office will answer questions about the newest figure.

sections.h2: What the Westchester County Clerk needs for a deed
sections.html:
Filing a deed means going through the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Its recording guide lists what to submit: a cover page generated in the county's PREP system, form TP-584, the RP-5217 transfer report, and a payment cover page that shows the fees and tax.

The state charges $2 for each $500 of the price, rounding up, and sellers usually pay. At $1,000,000 or more, a one to three family house or condo picks up an extra one percent mansion tax. Clerk's staff can't write a deed or give advice about one, so your attorney handles the document.

sections.h2: Selling with a lien or an open tax balance
sections.html:
An unpaid tax bill won't stop a sale, but it must be cleared when you close. Start by asking the Receiver of Taxes for a written balance. A lien is handled differently from an ordinary bill: it can't be paid online, so someone has to bring the payment to the Tax Office at 177 Hillside Avenue or send it by check made out to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes. Your closing attorney normally arranges this and takes the amount from your proceeds.

The Receiver has no power to waive a penalty, so a late bill costs what it costs. If you are behind and the house needs work you can't afford, a direct purchase by a cash buyer can pay the balance at the table and still leave you something. Compare that figure with what a listing would bring after commission, repairs and the months of carrying costs.

When a village bill applies as well as the town bill, collect both. The village office, not the town, sets the due dates for village taxes, so call that Village Hall for its schedule.

Start with the property condition disclosure statement required by Real Property Law section 462. The buyer must receive it before any binding contract is signed.

  • Certificates of occupancy or completion for finished space, and permit records for recent work.
  • Town, county and school tax bills, plus a village bill if you live in a village.
  • A lender payoff letter and details of any lien.
  • Your STAR status, since the state asks owners to close a registration after a sale.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip showings and repair negotiations, but title work, payoff and recording still take time. Ask for a written closing date and proof of funds with every offer.

faqs.q: Do village homes in Greenburgh use the town Building Department?
faqs.a: Generally not. The town department handles complaints only in the unincorporated part of Greenburgh. For a house in a village such as Tarrytown, ask the village hall about permits and due dates.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof in Greenburgh?
faqs.a: Yes. A roof covering replacement on a one or two family house needs a building permit with drawings, and a structural change needs plans from a New York State architect or engineer.

faqs.q: Can the next owner run a short-term rental from a Greenburgh house?
faqs.a: Short-term rentals aren't a permitted use in any residential zoning district. A buyer with that plan should confirm with the Building Department before closing.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Greenburgh sale?
faqs.a: State tax is $2 for every $500 of price. The one percent mansion tax starts at $1,000,000 for one to three family homes and condos, and the buyer pays it.

faqs.q: Where do Greenburgh property tax payments go?
faqs.a: To the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue, which collects for the county, town, fire districts and ten school districts. Village residents follow their village's own schedule.
